original_value: In this paper, the distributed filtering problem is addressed for a class of discrete-time stochastic systems over a sensor network with a given topology, susceptible to suffering deception attacks, launched by potential adversaries, which can randomly succeed or not with a known success probability, which is not necessarily the same for the different sensors. The system model integrates some random imperfections and features that are frequently found in real networked environments, namely: (1) fading measurements; (2) multiplicative noises in both the state and measurement equations; and (3) sensor additive noises cross-correlated with each other and with the process noise. According to the network communication scheme, besides its own local measurements, each sensor receives the measured outputs from its adjacent nodes. Based on such measurements, a recursive algorithm is designed to obtain the least-squares linear filter of the state. Thereafter, each sensor receives the filtering estimators previously obtained by its adjacent nodes, and these estimators are all fused to obtain the desired distributed filter as the minimum mean squared error matrix-weighted linear combination of them. The theoretical results are illustrated by a simulation example, where the efficiency of the developed distributed estimation strategy is discussed in terms of the error variances.

result.paraphrase: This paper tackles distributed filtering for a class of discrete-time stochastic systems on a sensor network with a prescribed topology that may be subject to deception attacks by potential adversaries; these attacks may succeed or fail at random, with known success probabilities that need not be identical across sensors. The model also incorporates random imperfections commonly encountered in real networked environments, including fading measurements, multiplicative noise in both the state and measurement equations, and sensor additive noises that are mutually cross-correlated and correlated with the process noise. Under the network communication protocol, each sensor receives not only its own local measurements but also the measured outputs from neighboring nodes. Using these observations, a recursive algorithm is developed to compute the least-squares linear state filter. Then each sensor collects the filtering estimates previously generated by its neighbors, and these estimates are fused to form the desired distributed filter as their minimum mean squared error matrix-weighted linear combination. The theoretical findings are demonstrated through a simulation example, and the effectiveness of the proposed distributed estimation method is evaluated via the error variances.
